decisions.place: Lower-right blank area, well below the closing
decisions.scan_shows: A thin dark stroke slopes down to the right, broadens at the bend, then curls down and slightly back left at its lower tip. There are no legible letters or label. C's context flags this unmarked target; the reading now marks that uncertainty explicitly and positions the curve in the lower-right blank area. H omits the mark.

notes: One typewritten, unsigned letter leaf, dated Massy le 3.11.1970 and addressed Cher Ferrand. The writer asks about receiving exposé XI for SGA 6 by the end of December and discusses publication without that exposé and a possible separate expository article. The page has no title, no manuscript pagination, no signature, no mathematical display and no explicit author doubt mark. The archive number 73 is recorded only as a comment. The right edge clips the body at diso plus a partial letter and at the final s of après; no unseen ns has been restored. Two overtyped positions in préférable are preserved. The lower-right curved mark is retained with a material/interpretive doubt. The long nearly vertical traces below cordialement and the pale paper mottling are treated as sheet condition, not authored writing. H's wrapper and descriptive note are metadata, not on-page text; their absence from reading.tex is not a collation difference.
math_reading_decisions: The references SGA 6 XI, SGA 6 and XI consist of ordinary typed capitals and numerals. No separate upper or lower rule, mathematical decoration, or doubled alphabet is present.
There is no mathematical argument or computation on this leaf; no proof check was performed.

completion: Complete page coverage: date, salutation, every body line and punctuation mark, both overprints, closing, isolated lower-right curve and archival number. The whole source image was viewed once for layout, then each supplied half once in order a and b. The four remaining open loci were each cropped once from the original, delivered in batches of three and one, and viewed once. No OCR, web research, other page, peer file or TeX engine was used.
